advisories.title: The collision universe never states its same-component exclusion, and entryShape.stableId's 'unique among LIVE entries per (stableId)' phrasing sits in tension with the multi-version coexistence pair both records require
advisories.detail: TC-ACCEPT requires a multi-version coexistence pair (same stableId+provenance, two versions, BOTH admitted — D-012 clause 7's goldens class) and RJ-1 rules the same-(ID,provenance) re-release 'a release'. But RJ-2's trigger quantifies over 'live names/aliases, live entries' MOUNTED ROOT COMMAND NAMES' with no same-stableId carve-out, the name field is 'unique among live names at admission', and the entryShape says stableId is 'unique among LIVE entries per (stableId)' — literally read, the second admission of the coexistence pair collides with the component's own first entry (name, mounted root, and stableId uniqueness all three). The intent is unambiguous — collision is everywhere framed cross-component (the hostile pairs, 'another component's mountedRootCommand'), and D-012 clause 7 lists coexistence as a positive class beside the collision negatives — but a fixture author implementing the triggers literally would refuse TC-ACCEPT's own required fixture. This is CARRIED v1 content (all three phrasings byte-identical from v1; the B5 widening merely extends the same unstated exclusion to mounted-root names), so it is not repair-injected and not a surviving named finding — it is new-by-my-sweep under the whole-artifact standard. One defining sentence closes it: collisions and the live-name/root-name uniqueness quantify over entries of a DIFFERENT stableId, and index entries are keyed per (stableId, version) with the component-binding uniqueness constraint holding per stableId.
